rules.when: A crewmate or scout is warranted but the work is small, explicit, and low risk: rote rename, formatting, typo, focused documentation edit, tiny fixture update, or a one-file/two-file bug with obvious acceptance criteria and no architecture/security implications.
rules.why: Spend the lightweight Luna or mini profile on bounded mechanical work instead of waking the strongest model.

rules.when: The task is ordinary scoped implementation or investigation: a contained feature, normal bug fix, backend test addition, documentation restructuring, or a review that spans several files but has clear boundaries.
rules.why: Use a balanced coding profile before spending the highest-reasoning pool.

rules.when: The task is large, ambiguous, high blast radius, or design-heavy: architecture/frozen-interface changes, broad refactors, difficult debugging, security-sensitive work, multi-project coordination, or work whose acceptance criteria must be discovered.
rules.why: Reserve stronger high-effort models for work where cheaper profiles are likely to burn more tokens by flailing.
